author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose a stuck button or axis
summary: Observe the exact held value, separate analog drift from missing release or duplicate bindings, test each source alone, and verify neutral state across lifecycle interruptions.
heroAlt: PCSX2 controller test gameplay frame selected for observing whether movement or an action remains active after release

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals

blocks.text: Observe the held value before resetting it

Disconnect every secondary controller and hide the touch overlay, then observe the remaining device in a live input monitor for thirty seconds without touching it. Record any nonzero axis and its drift range. Press and release each button once, then repeat while pausing, backgrounding, reconnecting, and rotating the device to find the transition that loses neutral state.

Do not use a large dead zone to hide a digital button that never releases. Dead zones address small analog drift, while an exact held value usually indicates duplicate ownership, a missing release event, or interrupted touch. Save the raw event trace before recalibrating so hardware wear is not confused with a lifecycle bug.
Prepare isolated device and lifecycle tests

items: Live input display ready before reproducing the stuck state.
Controller and touch profiles exported independently.
Dead-zone, turbo, and macro values recorded.
Capture thirty seconds of neutral raw input, then log press and release values while each secondary controller and touch source is disconnected.
Reproduce the suspected transition—touch cancellation, pause, background, reconnect, or rotation—while holding exactly one known input.

blocks.text: Classify the stuck state by how it clears

items: 1. Leave all controls untouched and record every non-neutral value.
2. Press and release the affected control slowly while watching transitions.
3. Disable touchscreen visibility for one pass without deleting its layout.
4. Test the physical controller alone, then disconnect it and observe the value.
5. Repeat an interrupted touch by leaving the app only after preserving evidence.
6. Inspect duplicate bindings, turbo, macros, and accessibility remappers.
7. Apply dead-zone correction only if the raw analog value truly wanders near center.
8. Cold-launch and repeat release, pause, resume, and reconnect checks.

blocks.text: A slowly changing stick value that appears in Android's tester points to calibration or hardware. A clean Android trace but stuck emulator state points to mapping, duplicated sources, or an input-backend transition. If the fault appears only after an overlay gesture or app resume, reproduce that sequence with the physical controller disconnected.

Every axis must settle inside the recorded neutral band and every button must return to zero after ordinary release, touch cancellation, pause/resume, and reconnect. Hold two inputs while performing each lifecycle transition to test release ordering. Repeat the sequence twice after saving the corrected mapping.

items: Digital buttons produce matched press and release transitions.
Analog axes settle inside the measured neutral boundary.
Background, resume, and device reconnect cannot preserve a stale held value.
A useful trace distinguishes slow analog drift from an exact retained value and names the lifecycle event after which neutral was lost.
Restart with the corrected map, repeat every transition twice, and require all axes and buttons to settle inside the recorded neutral band.
Raw drift remains outside the tester dead zone: service or replace the controller.
Only touch interruption sticks: capture the lifecycle reproduction for an app report.
Two sources hold one function: remove the duplicate owner.
A title retains movement with neutral tester values: investigate game state or save-state behavior.

blocks.text: Return calibration and bindings to baseline

Remove the temporary isolation profile, reconnect one source at a time, and restore the original calibration values. If drift returns with one physical device, leave that device disconnected rather than distorting the shared map for all controllers. If a lost release returns only with touch, reload the original overlay and preserve the event trace for a bug report.
Clearing the symptom is not the same as finding its source

Neutral behavior is a sequence, not one screenshot. Some devices recenter differently after reconnect, and Android can assign a new descriptor while retaining the same product name. Store the resting range and failure transition with the hardware identity; retest after controller firmware, input-backend, or app lifecycle changes.
Use Android's one-press and analog-drift checks
